page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused server configuration designed for CPU-intensive computing tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a 16-core, 32-thread Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs supported by 260 MB of shared L3 cache and 64 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for advanced vector and matrix instruction sets, such as AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and Intel AMX (Tile, INT8), as well as hardware cryptographic extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent compute and data processing capabilities. The instance achieves strong results in Geekbench 6 single-core (2,196.0) and multi-core (16,926.0) testing, with top-tier throughput in text processing (2,919.0) and image processing. Single-threaded data handling tests also demonstrate high efficiency, scoring 33.81 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.44 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Small-scale CPU-based language model text generation reaches top-tier throughput at 417.13 tokens per second, while general-purpose multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark overall scores (40,815.66), and database operations place in the average middle percentile tier.

The c4-highcpu-32 includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, requiring compute setups to rely entirely on external network-attached storage volumes. Memory allocation is modest relative to core count, meaning data-dense in-memory architectures may face memory constraints despite high raw processing power. From a resource perspective, the instance prioritizes dedicated core density and vector acceleration over memory footprint.

Given its performance characteristics, the server is suitable for CPU-bound batch processing, static web serving (benchmarked at 53.01 GB/sec), software compilation, text analytics, and lightweight machine learning inference pipelines that can leverage Intel AMX instructions.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-32 is a compute-oriented virtual server powered by a dedicated 16-core, 32-thread Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. It delivers 32 vCPUs alongside 64 GB of memory, equating to a 1:2 core-to-memory allocation, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The architecture includes Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions for vector and matrix mathematics, though it includes neither local storage nor discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong performance in single- and multi-core Geekbench metrics, top-tier scores in text processing and small-model language inference, alongside average multi-core stress ratings. Static web serving throughput reaches 53.01 GB/sec, and compression throughput is robust. The platform is optimized for CPU-heavy tasks such as code compilation, automated batch jobs, web tier workloads, and integer or matrix-driven inference operations that do not demand extensive RAM capacity.
